title: A serious illness conversation template with prompts and skills training on two hospital wards: a feasibility study
abstract: Objective: to test whether a serious illness conversation template with prompts, a skills session and feedback can be delivered on two wards, and whether note quality and family-reported outcomes can be measured, before a stepped-wedge trial. Design: six-month non-randomised feasibility study with progression criteria. Results will follow data collection.
introduction: Prompts increase documented conversations, but evidence conflicts on whether notes improve in quality, and few studies measure what patients and families experience.
methods: Triggered patients on two wards; template, prompts, skills session and feedback; delivery, rater agreement, family response, documentation and quality measured against progression criteria.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present delivery, kappa, family response and descriptive change against the progression criteria.
discussion: The discussion will judge the progression criteria and state whether and how a stepped-wedge trial should proceed.
limitations: Two wards, no comparison group, small family sample.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim an effect of the template.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility studies, adapted for a non-randomised design
summary: Feasibility report structure with results left empty.
